rendered: The document reports a sulfur loading of 35[1] wt % sulfur, completely confined in the micropores of the carbon spheres. The process was a low-temperature, isothermal vapor-phase infiltration: the prepared carbon powder is infiltrated with sulfur at 175 °C[2] for 1 h[3]. The authors contrast this with melt-infiltration methods that take a long time, which they describe as slower and less scalable.
